stem.en: Kabir deposits the whole lunch as one long chain, ignoring the brancher, and saves the coins branching would have cost. What has he lost?

text.en: Ends. A single chain has one end to add to and one to withdraw from. Tomorrow, when he needs sugar fast, the bank can only pay out one bead at a time from one place.

feedback.en: Stored, yes. Usable quickly, no. The shape of the store sets the speed of withdrawal.
A long alpha chain is starch, and it is perfectly stable. Plants store it that way. It is just slow to open.

text.en: He has saved coins and lost nothing.

feedback.en: He has saved a few coins now and will pay in speed later, in a sprint, which is tomorrow's game.

explanation.en: Every branch is an extra door. Deposit and withdrawal both go through doors. A tree with a hundred doors moves sugar a hundred times faster than a chain with one.
